thread:
anya: Opening a short follow-up thread from today's runtime roadmap Q&A. Post quick clarifications or items to action.

john: Two quick things: how does the new adaptive soft-degrade work when GPU pools are saturated? We want predictable fallbacks.

sam: Soft-degrade is a policy that shifts traffic to lower-cost model variants and increases batching aggressiveness progressively. It uses a per-tenant signal and a global safety throttle. We'll expose a `soft_degrade_mode` toggle and `kernel_fallback_ratio` metric to measure how much traffic falls back.

liam: To add: fallbacks prefer quantized-compatible kernels first, then smaller model variants. We also plan a grace period to avoid flip-flopping under oscillating load.

claire: Any change to per-request quota semantics? Some customers worried about hidden rate limits when batching increases.

sam: No silent limits. We surface a new metric `effective_rps` that shows requests/sec after batching semantics, and `per_route_throttle` for any active throttles. The API will return headers when soft-degrade or throttles apply.

anya: Kernel question: status on fused kernels and the Ampere corner-case?

liam: Fused kernels landed in an internal branch. Ampere codegen corner case reproducible on specific driver+cuda combo; kernel team has a patch ready, testing on the testbed. Until QA clears it, fused kernels are behind runtime_v3 feature flag.

deploy-bot: deploy: scheduled canary for runtime_v3 on canary-cluster-1  ETA 1h.

john: Can we get a short playbook for customers showing how to opt in and what to monitor?

sam: Yes  I'll add a two-page playbook: opt-in steps, `kernel_fallback_ratio`, `batch_fill_pct`, `kv_cache_hit_rate`, and a quick runbook for rollbacks. Also scheduling office hours next week for customer walkthroughs.

anya: Action items: sam to publish the playbook and example header responses; liam to post kernel test status; I'll schedule office hours and post invites. Thanks all! :handshake:
